newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee dips on late dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee dips on late dollar demand.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee lost ground in late trading and closed soft on demand for dollars, which dealers said was caused by import covering and speculation.
The rupee closed at 57.03 after opening at 57.00 and moving to 56.93 early in the day. The rupee closed at 56.95 on Friay.

"There was a little commercial demand for dollars in the afternoon. But there could also have been some speculative buying, due to low call rates and the overseas strength of the dollar," said a Commercial Bank dealer.
Call money closed at 13 percent after moving between 12 and 15.5 percent, dealers said.

"Despite some volatility caused by investors going to the secondary Treasury Bill market, the recent easing of monetary policy should keep money below a maximum of about 17 percent," said a Bank of Ceylon dealer.
The Central Bank recently permitted exporters foreign exchange loans, and cut the statutory reserve to 14 percent from 15.
